plan: Given my private value of $3, bidding higher than $3 would result in a loss if I win the auction. To maximize profit, I should bid less than or equal to my value. Since this is a first-price auction and there is no history to learn from, I'll bid $3, ensuring no loss if I win. This approach minimizes risk and aligns with the goal of maximizing profit over rounds, even though this is a single round.

Given my private value of $45, I aim to bid just below my value to maximize potential profit while maintaining a competitive edge. A bid slightly below $45 reduces the risk of overpaying if I win. I anticipate others may bid close to their values, thus I will bid $43. This provides a buffer for profit if I win and increases my chances of winning against slightly lower bids.

Given my high private value of $48, I aim to bid aggressively to maximize my chance of winning while ensuring a good profit margin. A bid slightly below my value, such as $40, balances winning probability and profit. This bid is competitive enough to outbid typical mid-range values other bidders may have, without risking overpayment.
